handbookNote: New Hampshire Notary Law -- RSA Chapter 455 (Notaries Public and Commissioners, 12 operative sections: 455:1, 2, 2-a, 3, 4, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 -- sections 455:5 to 455:10 repealed 2006) plus RSA Chapter 456-B (New Hampshire's Revised Uniform Law on Notarial Acts, 19 operative sections: 456-B:1 through 456-B:11, several lettered -- 2-a, 2-b, 6-a, 8-a through 8-e), ~31 operative sections combined, fetched directly from the official New Hampshire General Court statute site (gc.nh.gov, the successor domain for gencourt.state.nh.us) 2026-08-16. CLASSIFICATION (confirmed): application-only -- there is no notary exam and no mandatory pre-commissioning training course; RSA 455:17 obligates the Secretary of State only to PREPARE and distribute an educational manual for notaries/justices of the peace, not to test or train them. This question bank is grounded, self-study/reference practice content, not exam prep in the licensing-exam sense. UNUSUAL FEATURES documented and tested: (1) notaries are appointed by the GOVERNOR, with the advice and consent of the EXECUTIVE COUNCIL (RSA 455:1) -- a state-level gubernatorial appointment, not a county-level or Secretary-of-State model; 5-year commission term; (2) applicants must be endorsed for appointment by TWO sitting notaries public AND one registered voter of the state (RSA 455:2) -- an unusual triple peer-vouching requirement; (3) NH's RULONA implementation includes a detailed remote online notarization framework at RSA 456-B:6-a (eff. Feb. 6, 2022) and a COVID-era-turned-permanent estate-planning remote-witnessing accommodation at RSA 456-B:2, VII. CONTENT DEPTH RATIONALE: 159 questions were generated across 7 topic buckets (Appointment/Application/Qualifications; Powers/Notarial Acts/Definitions; Fees & Commissioners of Deeds; Notarial Acts Across Jurisdictions & Validity; Remote Online Notarization; Certificates/Short Forms/Stamp/Journal; Misconduct/Manual/Education), each question citing a specific RSA 455:xx or 456-B:x section/paragraph -- landing within the confirmed ~150-180 target ceiling for this statute's real content depth, per the project's 'better nothing than nonsense' rule (no padding/filler/trivial-reword questions). PRICING: $0.99 (99 cents) -- consistent with this project's other application-only notary states (no confirmed graded assessment of any kind), priced well below the $9.99 tier reserved for states with an actual licensing exam.
